title: fix(plugin-auth)!: a password reset ends what the account added before it
body:

_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D1WDVL9JpCQhTUF97fpymtZ)_

Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户在登录页用邮件或短信重置密码后：账号此前的 API 密钥被吊销、已关联的第三方登录被解除（以前都保留）；正常修改密码不动它们，但会给账号邮箱发一封提醒，列出仍然有效的密钥和关联登录。
- 延续上一轮「改密即结束此前签发的访问」这一规则：账号第一次被设上密码（重置、管理员设置、邀请）也算一次改密，此前发出的自动登录验证链接和免密登录链接随之作废。
- 依赖旧 API 密钥的脚本在账号主人重置密码后会被拒，需要重新生成或在密钥列表里恢复；问题可直接撤回本次合并恢复原行为。
- 无

## What changes

A password reset ends what the account added before it, and a password change reminds the account what it keeps. One rule and one clock: everything here reads the credential clock that `readCredentialChangedAt` / `issuedBeforeCredentialChange` already provide.

**A completed self-service reset ends what the account added.** On success of `POST /reset-password` or `POST /phone-number/reset-password`, for the account the before-hook named, the global after-hook (`password-reset-ends-added-access.ts`) ends:

| What the account added | On this build | What the reset does |
|---|---|---|
| API keys (`sys_api_key`) | present | every unrevoked key is written `revoked: true` (paged, a key read twice is an error, never a loop); no `revoked_reason`, the same as a key its owner revokes |
| Linked sign-in accounts (`sys_account`, any provider other than `credential`: social, generic OAuth, SSO; `/link-social` is mounted) | present | deleted through better-auth's internal adapter, so its account-delete hooks run; no unlink record is written, so a provider links again as it did the first time |
| Passkeys | **not present**: the `passkeys` flag is wired to no plugin and no passkey store is mounted | nothing to end; named in the module header so a store mounted later joins the list |

A reset that does not complete ends nothing. A read or write that fails is not swallowed: the reset answers an error, and the next completed reset ends what is left.

**A password change keeps them and reminds.** `POST /change-password` ends none of these. When the account still holds a key or a linked sign-in account afterwards, the account's address is sent the new built-in `auth.password_changed_notice` through the existing email service (`sendTemplate`, `identityMail`, no new transport), naming each key and provider. Best-effort, like the email-change notice: it never fails the change. plugin-email ships it in en-US, zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES (`BUILTIN_AUTH_TEMPLATES` 32 → 36 rows), and core's `PLATFORM_REQUESTED_BARE_NAMES_BY_TYPE.email_template` names it beside the other eight.

**Administrator and operator resets.** `POST /admin/set-user-password` with `revokeSessionsAndKeys` on (the default) and `os user set-password` already ended sessions and keys through `forced-reset-revocation.ts`; that module now also unlinks every non-credential sign-in account. The response's `revoked` gains `signInAccounts`, the ledger row gains `revokedSignInAccounts`, and the operator outcome gains `signInAccountsUnlinked`. An administrator who passes `revokeSessionsAndKeys: false` asks for a routine reset: that switch is the code's reason not to treat it as a self-service reset, and it still ends nothing. The one-step invitation door only ever sets the password of an account with no sign-in and no standing grant, so it has nothing of this to end.

**An account's first password, set onto an account that was already there, is a password change.** `readCredentialChangedAt` used to read a credential row not written over since its creation as "never changed". It now tells the two apart by when the row was created against the account (`sys_user.created_at`, read through the same internal adapter's `findUserById`):
- created within the same 1 s window as the account: a sign-up with a password, an administrator's create-user, an import, the one-step door creating a new account. Not a change;
- created onto an account that already existed: either reset door creating the first password (`resetCredentialPassword` creates the row), `/admin/set-user-password`, the one-step door setting the first password of an existing account, `/set-initial-password`. A change, at the row's creation.

An account whose creation cannot be read is judged as one that was already there (fail closed); a reader without `findUserById` answers "issued before" (fail closed). The operator reset refuses an account with no local password, so it never creates a first one.

**Links that sign in follow the same clock.** The before-hook now ends, when minted before the account's credential change:
- a `/verify-email` token without `updateTo`, on a deployment with `emailVerification.autoSignInAfterVerification: true`. It answers what a never-issued token answers (`401 INVALID_TOKEN` or the `error=INVALID_TOKEN` redirect). With auto-sign-in off, the link signs nobody in and the vendor judges it as before;
- a magic link at `GET /magic-link/verify`. Its issue time is its `magic-link:TOKEN` verification row's creation. It answers the vendor's own never-issued redirect and opens no session. A non-plain `storeToken` or an unreadable row ends the link (fail closed).

Tokens minted after the change work as usual.

### Read first (by risk)

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts`: the `readCredentialChangedAt` hunk (the first-password discriminator) and `endMagicLinkIssuedBeforeCredentialChange` (its fail-closed branches).
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts` → `password-reset-ends-added-access.ts`: the reset-door branch runs after the password write; a failure there answers the requester an error although the password was written.
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/forced-reset-revocation.ts`: the new sign-in account arm (the credential row is skipped by `provider_id`).

## Tests

Every new case runs through the real routes: AuthManager + AuthPlugin on Hono over SQLite ObjectQL, the vendor's own endpoints, a captured mail and SMS service, and keys admitted through core's `resolveApiKeyAdmission`.

- `password-reset-ends-added-access.test.ts` (new, 8 cases): the emailed reset and the texted reset end the key and the github link (control: the new password signs in, a key minted after admits); a reset that does not complete ends nothing; a refused write answers ≥ 500; a change keeps both and sends the notice (`apiKeyCount: 1`, `apiKeys: 'ci-deploy'`, `signInAccounts: 'github'`); an account holding neither is sent nothing; admin with the switch off ends nothing, on gives `{ apiKeys: 1, signInAccounts: 1, failed: 0, complete: true }`; the operator reset gives `signInAccountsUnlinked: 1`.
- `credential-change-ends-prior-access.test.ts`: the clock's unit case; a sign-up-with-password control; the emailed reset, the texted reset and `/admin/set-user-password` each creating the first password end an email-change link minted before; a verification link with auto-sign-in (with the auto-sign-in-off control); a magic link (no session, never-issued redirect; one minted after signs in).
- `invitation-one-step-acceptance-34257.test.ts`: the one-step door setting the first password of an existing account reads a change; one creating the account with it reads none.
- plugin-email: the notice in all four locales (subject, what stays active, the reset road, no "safe to ignore" footer, no en-US text in other locales) and its render pinned in `builtin-auth-render-identity.test.ts`.

## Acceptance notes

- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION** of a pending release note: `.changeset/credential-change-ends-prior-access.md` said "An account's first password is not a change." That sentence is now false for a first password set onto an existing account, so this PR deletes it; this PR's changeset states the new rule. `check-empty-changeset` is red on that file by design.
- A password reset revokes the account's keys **without** a `revoked_reason`, so the owner can restore one from the API Keys list, the same as a key the owner revoked. The administrator's forced reset keeps `admin_password_reset`, which only a platform administrator restores. This is a choice the rule did not fix, raised as an open question.
- A reset unlinks **every** non-credential sign-in account, including the one the account signed up with. Signing in with it again links it again when the provider's address matches (implicit linking writes no unlink record here).
- When the after-hook's ending fails after the password write, the reset answers an error although the new password is in place. This is deliberate: an ending that does not happen must not read as success. The requester resets again.
- The email-OTP reset (`/email-otp/reset-password`) is not wired on this build, so there is nothing for it.
